findings.title: Signed integer overflow in tilde-stretching multiplication (af_latin_stretch_top_tilde / af_latin_stretch_bottom_tilde)
findings.message: In the tilde-unflattening scaling code, each point's y-coordinate is rescaled with a raw C expression `( ( p->y - min_y ) * target_height / height ) + min_y`. The comment claims 'we are never dealing with large numbers and can thus avoid `FT_MulFix`', but `p->y - min_y` and `target_height` are both `FT_Pos` (a signed long) values derived from font outline coordinates, which for malformed/fuzzed fonts can reach values large enough that their product overflows a signed long before the division by `height` reduces it back down. Signed integer overflow is undefined behavior in C and was flagged by OSS-Fuzz (issue 471525116) as UBSan-detected signed-integer-overflow in this multiplication. The same unguarded multiplication pattern was copied to the newly added bottom-tilde counterpart (af_latin_stretch_bottom_tilde) when that function was introduced later by analogy to this one. The eventual fix wraps the multiplication with `MUL_LONG()`, which performs the multiplication in a wider/safe way and avoids UB while producing an INT_MAX/INT_MIN saturation result instead of wrapping.
findings.suggestion: Do not assume the diacritic scaling values are always small. Wrap the multiplication with a saturating/overflow-safe helper such as `MUL_LONG()` (and use `ADD_LONG`/`SUB_LONG` for the surrounding addition/subtraction) instead of performing raw signed multiplication that can overflow for malformed or extreme font outlines.

ground_truth.root_cause: The multiplication `(p->y - min_y) * target_height` was written with a comment claiming the operands are always small enough to avoid overflow, without any actual bounds validation. This assumption does not hold for arbitrary/fuzzed font glyph coordinates, allowing the signed multiplication to overflow FT_Pos (a signed long), which is undefined behavior in C and can yield incorrect or attacker-influenced results.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Signed integer overflow in tilde-stretching multiplication (af_latin_stretch_top_tilde / af_latin_stretch_bottom_tilde)
